title: Tiered warm-up & probe-isolation postmortem: reactive scale-down causing latency spikes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: On 2026-01-17, between 03:10–03:42 UTC we observed repeated customer-facing latency spikes for the hosted inference tier. Symptoms were high 95th/99th token latency and brief request timeouts for ~7% of requests to a high-throughput model route. The symptom correlated with a sequence of aggressive scale-down events that reduced available worker instances below the warm-working set, exposing cold-starts. This incident affected both hosted API customers and a small number of Dedicated clusters running the same autoscaling policy template.

What happened (short): A miscalibrated probe fusion heuristic caused KEDA's Redis-length scaler to be over-attenuated while the HPA's percentile-based latency probe admitted noisy spikes as the norm. The combined decision logic favored scale-down (false negative for load) and evicted worker pods from the warm pool. When traffic resumed, requests hit workers without warmed KV caches and cold-attention kernels, producing high tail latency and timeouts.

Scope & impact: ~7% of requests to the affected route experienced tail latencies > 4.5s (baseline ~120–200ms). Customer error rate increased by ~0.8 percentage points for 32 minutes. No data loss, but SLA windows for several higher-tier customers were degraded leading to two on-call escalations.

Systems involved: KEDA scaler (Redis stream length trigger), HPA (custom metrics server with percentile aggregation), warm-pool controller (probe eviction and warm cohort management), serving runtime (KV cache priming and kernel selection), control plane routing (fallback policy).
root_cause_summary: Two independent signal-processing regressions combined: 1) the percentile aggregator for latency (custom metrics exporter) defaulted to a 30s rolling window and used an arithmetic smoothing that treated transient spikes as persistent, lowering the observed demand after compaction; 2) KEDA's scaler configuration had its recent debounce/backoff parameters reduced in a prior change, allowing scaledown decisions to execute with insufficient hysteresis. The warm-pool eviction logic treated probe misses during scale-down as a signal that pods were idle and evicted them aggressively. The emergent behavior: system underprovisioned exactly when traffic rose, producing cold-start amplification.
mitigation_taken_during_incident: 1) Temporarily disabled automated scale-down for the affected fleet (runtime-1.21 tag) to preserve warm workers. 2) Increased HPA percentile aggregation window to 90s for the impacted route. 3) Manually cleared eviction markers so warm pool pods were retained. 4) Rolled back the recent KEDA debounce change to restore prior backoff behavior. These steps restored tail latency to baseline within ~9 minutes of action.
long_term_mitigation: 1) Implement per-cohort tiered warm pools (hot/warm/cold) so immediate requests are routed to hot pods and warm pods are used as second-tier with soft-eviction rules. 2) Add a probe-isolation flag that forces probe samples from control-plane health-checks to be excluded from demand calculations (prevents probe noise imprinting). 3) Fuse signals from KEDA (queue-length) and HPA (percentile latency) with a small rule engine that prefers conservative decisions during rising traffic and enforces minimum hold times post-scale-down. 4) Add an adaptive probe-backoff algorithm that increases debounce when variance is high. 5) Add e2e test harness that simulates traffic spikes and verifies warm-pool retention under the new heuristics.
action_items: AI-1: Implement probe-isolation flag in warm-pool controller; ensure control-plane probes are tagged and excluded from percentile metrics. Owner: @liam.oconnor. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-02-05.
AI-2: Tiered warm-pool design doc + API (hot/warm/cold) and routing rules. Owner: @maya. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-02-12.
AI-3: Signal-fusion rule engine prototype: prefer queue-length OR rising-percentile (with min-hold) before scale-down. Owner: @arjun.singh. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-02-08.
AI-4: Revert/guard KEDA debounce change with feature flag and add automated guardrail tests (unit+integration). Owner: @natalie. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-02-03.
AI-5: Expand observability: add per-route warm-pool size and probe-noise scoreboard to Console dashboards + alert when warm-pool < threshold. Owner: @elaine. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-02-15.

AI-6: Runbook update: create step-by-step for ‘aggressive scale-down with cold-start tail’ including rollback of scale-down and warm-pool retention steps. Owner: @sre_oncall. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-02-01.
AI-7: Create e2e load test simulating bursty traffic patterns and validate that no more than 0.5% of requests exceed 2s tail under configured policies. Owner: @perf_lab. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-02-22.
AI-8: Post-deploy monitoring: run 2-week observation window after runtime-1.21 changes; produce analytics report on scale-up/scale-down frequency. Owner: @ops_analytics. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-01.
timeline: 2026-01-17 03:10 UTC: First alert - HPA percentile > threshold and KEDA triggered a scale-down window.
2026-01-17 03:14 UTC: Tail latency spikes observed; on-call alerted. Marked as incident.
2026-01-17 03:20 UTC: First mitigation - disabled scale-down for affected fleet. Partial improvement.
2026-01-17 03:28 UTC: Rolled back KEDA debounce change. Warm pods began to reappear.
2026-01-17 03:36 UTC: Full traffic back to normal tail latencies. Monitoring continued for 30m.
evidence_links: Metrics exporter change that introduced percentile compaction: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-exporter/commit/3b9a7f2
comments: 2026-01-17 04:12 - Maya Chen: Initial post-incident notes added. We should prioritize probe isolation so control-plane activity doesn't contaminate demand signals.

2026-01-18 09:23 - Liam O'Connor: Confirmed root cause locally: the percentile aggregator applies exponential compaction when memory pressure > 0, which was active due to a side-effect of the metrics exporter shipping. Reverting compaction restores expected percentiles.
2026-01-25 16:45 - Natalie Rivera: KEDA debounce guard with feature-flag landed in staging; integration tests added. See PR #1467.
2026-01-28 11:02 - Elaine Park: Dashboard tile for warm-pool size added to console branch; will be on staging tomorrow.
2026-02-01 08:17 - SRE oncall: Runbook entry merged. Add phone escalation step for customers with SLA >99.9%.
2026-02-02 14:00 - Arjun Singh: Signal-fusion prototype benchmark shows 18% fewer unnecessary scale-downs in synthetic workloads; pushing to canary next week.
lessons_learned: 1) Independent small regressions in signal processing can combine non-linearly — testing must include multi-signal chaos scenarios. 2) Warm-pool eviction policies must be conservative by default; soft-eviction and per-cohort policies reduce customer exposure. 3) Observability gaps (no warm-pool metric on Console previously) slowed diagnosis. 4) Feature flags and integrated tests for debounce behavior would have prevented the rapid rollout of a harmful change.
postmortem_notes: Ownership: This incident is owned by autoscale-resilience (cross-team). Action items assigned. We will run a follow-up review after the tiered warm-pool prototype is canaried. If the e2e load test indicates any regression, we will pause further autoscaler changes until protective tests are added to the CI gate.
